Everything else is a **command**: `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` as its owner declares (`body.state` for every avatar-acting verb; `emitter.state` for `toggle_beam`, whose `actor` is the seat's beam id) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The Adapter sends `set_move_intent` **only on change** of octant or `run`, with the stick quantised to 8 octants under `MOVE_DEADZONE` = 0.25 and `OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG` = 5°. In one frame it submits `set_move_intent` **before** any command (submission order is the P2 apply order — the kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source) from it, and callers never choose it, delegated ruling R2 — so a stop and a `begin_*` in the same frame apply in that order, PC-7). It sends `set_aim` when the quantised value differs from `last_acked` by **≥ 1/128 turn (2.8°)**, **or** the aim source changed (mouse ↔ stick ↔ keys), **or** `live` changed, **or** a settle condition holds (inside the threshold but differing at all, for `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` = 6) — **rate-limited to one per `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL` = 3 ticks**. At rest that is zero sends; a sweep is ≤ 20 sends/s, far inside `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`. **No input buffering**: `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` = 0; a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY`, honestly; nothing is queued for "after". *Rationale:* buffering hides the sim's answer behind a presentation guess; Zomboid's immediacy is the model. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Zero buffering is a recorded, deliberate trade, not an oversight:** an `interact` for a `CHANNEL` verb pressed one to three ticks before the move keys are up is rejected `MOVING` (PC-7) and costs one honest re-press; the same-tick case (release W and press E in one frame) is solved by ordering, not by buffering (intents are submitted first and validation reads `intent_octant`, PC-7). Adapter-side lever, **off at MVP**: `CHANNEL_BEGIN_GRACE_TICKS` (0–3, default **0**) would hold a `begin_*` press until the Adapter's own last-submitted octant is NONE for at most that many ticks; a playtest finding of "my weld never starts" is the trigger to raise it. *Ignored-input cues (accessibility):* four presses are dropped by Adapter-local knowledge alone and play one short dull cue (`cue_input_ignored`, the same id for all four, no visual, never read from a sim result): `toggle_beam` inside the rate-limit window (PC-5), `interact` with no focused object, `run` while `carry_ref ≠ none`, and `run` while the player's own inventory view shows a HEAVY item stowed (`stowed_heavy`, user ruling D18 and D.4; the name is the one Suit & Equipment publishes, registry `stowed_heavy`, and the earlier `heavy_stowed` is retired *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, general rule G1)*; it is the consequence of the player's own stow command, not a hidden reading) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D18)*. The cue is Adapter-local and so cannot reveal a sim answer; `run` under Suit's cap gets none (the cap is Suit's state, shown by the breath and warmth readings).
126	
127	*Immediate acknowledgement and the pre-play token (CR-4).* On submit the Adapter pre-plays **body and sound only, never the effect**: the hand's switch animation, the tool click, the bar starting. Each pre-play is keyed by an opaque integer **`correlation`** the Adapter attaches to the command (a per-Adapter counter; the kernel echoes it unchanged in the result or rejection event; `submit()` stays void and fire-and-forget, and the kernel, not the caller, stamps `seq`) in a `correlation → pre-play token` map, so a late result cancels the right pre-play *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. The beam light is the one object that is not pre-played (PC-5). **Rejection classes** (declared by each verb's owner, Interaction's GDD): *immediate* reasons — `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BUSY`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`, every admission reason — **withdraw the ack at once** (the sound stops, the bar vanishes within one frame of the result); the free-lie-detector case of Pillar 4 (a device the player perceives as broken or fixed) is **not a rejection**: the command is `Applied` and the channel resolves to a `PRECONDITION` outcome (Interaction, KRN:96), so the ack is never withdrawn — the work loop and the bar continue until Interaction's channel state signals the outcome. **The ack frame for a command whose channel will complete and one whose channel will resolve to `PRECONDITION` must be pixel- and sound-identical.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system)* Rejection is never a shake (C9, HR-13).
128	
129	*Non-audio counterpart (HUD-owned; reduced to the MOVING tell).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated CD ruling, HUD re-review K43)* Every negative cue was audio-only, so deaf and hard-of-hearing players got none, and nothing taught the three core rules (channels need stillness, prompts need light, destructive verbs need a hold). The only non-audio counterpart at MVP is the pre-press tell for a `begin_*` press that the actor's **own** state would block (`MOVING`): Interaction's `focus_view.press_blocked_moving`, drawn by HUD as a hollow keycap on `CHANNEL` and `HOLD_CONFIRM` plates (Interaction IA-41, AC-IA-142). The Adapter publishes **no** `input_ignored_view(seat)` and no reason class to the HUD: a visible response to a `NOT_LIT` (or any subject-dependent) press would tell the player something is at the unlit subject, the unlit-subject oracle Pillar 3 forbids, so the glyph dim on `NOT_LIT`, `BUSY`-by-other-seat, `OUT_OF_RANGE` and `INVALID_TARGET` presses is refused; the HUD still holds the restored keycap for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` on a plate Interaction has already shown (HUD HS-41). The other ignored-input cues (`cue_input_ignored`: `toggle_beam` in its window, `interact` with no focus, `run` while carrying) stay audio-only at MVP; a non-audio counterpart for them is deferred to `design/accessibility-requirements.md` (Open Question 26) and must not key on subject existence or lighting. **First-use hints are refused**: no caption, no Settings "seen" flag, no "reset profile" interaction (HUD HS-57, anti-pillar 4; teaching belongs to the world, Cryo Bay onboarding). **Playtest metric:** ≥ 80 % of first-time testers complete the first weld within two attempts; a miss reopens the Cryo Bay onboarding (HUD OQ-HS-29), not the rules and not a HUD hint.
130	
131	*Resync rule (one rule, five triggers).* The Adapter keeps `last_acked` per intent type and must **resend its current quantised value, bypassing the change filter once**, when: (i) an intent result arrives `Rejected(STALE)` (kernel Edge Cases: a stale "stop" otherwise leaves the actor moving); (ii) the kernel leaves `PAUSED` (CR-16 rejects intents immediately while paused, so a release during a pause was lost); (iii) `LOADING → RUNNING`; (iv) window focus returns, or the active gamepad reconnects; (v) **`TRANSFER`**: the actor's `body_of_actor` changes, i.e. a pod arrival (`IN_POD →` the locomotion-class member) or a section-detach body transfer, because the new body's first tick must act on the keys physically held *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: pod arrival and body transfer were handled only as an ad-hoc "treated as trigger iii" in Edge Cases)*. For a hold-mode channel it compares the actual button state to the last submitted one on each of those and submits `cancel_channel` if the button is up. **Window focus loss** submits `set_move_intent {NONE}` and `cancel_channel` if channelling, and marks every held action released; **the loss of the active gamepad** (a disconnect, mid-weld included) is treated identically (the same zero intent and cancel, the held pad actions released, the keyboard and mouse stay live, and a reconnect resyncs under trigger iv), and **the click or key press that returns window focus is consumed by the Adapter** and never reaches a binding (an LMB alias of `interact` would otherwise fire on refocus) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Invariant (testable): the sim's intent equals the player's hands within one tick of the kernel being `RUNNING`.
132	
133	**PC-3. Movement: ship-local, 8-way, two gaits, whole base pixels per tick, no physics body.** Movement is in the **body frame** (pipeline C2); the interior never shows ship motion. Input is **8-way**; gait is the `run` action, never stick deflection. *Rationale:* the noise cost of running (PC-10) must be a deliberate input, not a thumb slip (Sirlin's test for a real decision), and analog speed would be a continuum of non-integer px/tick, which PR-4 rule 3 forbids at camera quantum 1.
134	
135	*Speeds — derivation.* The pipeline routes "whole base px per tick when the quantum is 1" (PR-4 rule 3) and asserts two build invariants on `v_max`: `LAG_CUT > v_max·τ_follow` → `v_max < 266 px/s`, **and** `0.30·L_h > v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX` at the default field → `0.18·v_max + 72 ≤ 108` → **`v_max < 200 px/s`**. The second binds (the gameplay-programmer's reading and the game-designer's coincide); the brief's 266 is not the operative bound. At `TICK_RATE` = 60 the whole-px/tick ladder is 60 / 120 / 180 / 240 px/s, so the integer ceiling is **3 px/tick = 180 px/s** (lag 32.4 px; 32.4 + 72 = 104.4 ≤ 108). The pipeline's placeholders 90 / 150 px/s are 1.5 / 2.5 px/tick — non-integer under its own routed rule — and are superseded (routed correction).
136	
137	| Knob | Value | px/s at 60 Hz | tiles/s | Why |
138	|---|---|---|---|---|
139	| `v_walk` (registry: `V_WALK`) | **2 px/tick** | 120 | 2.5 | Deliberate but not tedious: the 13-tile default field crosses in ≈ 5 s; the boarding rhythm's pace is set by doors and reading. 1 px/tick recorded as the playtest alternative |
140	| `v_run` (registry: `V_RUN`) | **3 px/tick** | 180 | 3.75 | The integer ceiling under the inner-box invariant; 1.5× walk reads with the forward lean (5.2) and never clamps the camera |
141	| `v_carry` (registry: `V_CARRY`) | **1 px/tick** | 60 | 1.25 | A module at chest height halves the walk; extraction under rising Attention is the sortie's tension, and the slowdown is *seen* (carry-walk cycle), never a hidden stat |
142	| `v_max` | = `v_run` | 180 | — | Read by the pipeline's G check |
143	
144	All speeds are in px/tick and are invalidated by a `TICK_RATE` change (kernel Open Question 12).
145	
146	*Kinematics (Body's mechanism, this GDD's contract — Body to confirm).* **The avatar has no physics body.** Ship Body runs a hand-rolled integer kinematic step `LocomotionStep.step(state, intent, collide: Callable)` — a pure `RefCounted`, headless-testable: `pos: Vector2i` (base px, body frame) plus `sub: Vector2i` in **1/256-px fixed point**; velocity from an 8-entry integer unit table (cardinal 256, **diagonal 181/256** per axis, so diagonal speed equals cardinal speed to 0.1 %); **axis-separated 1-px AABB sweeps**, x then y every tick, against Layout's integer footprint rectangles, consumed as `SIMULATION` data (walls 24 px deep under the up-screen convention, closed door leaves, props, machinery) — sliding along a wall falls out of axis separation; `sub` **resets to zero on stop**; the foot box is **16 × 8 base px**, horizontally centred on the foot origin, which is the box's top row (`[pos.x − 8, pos.x + 8) × [pos.y, pos.y + 8)`; registry `foot_box`, `FOOT_BOX_W`, `FOOT_BOX_H`). Consequence: the avatar's position is a **pure function of the command stream and the layout**, so the kernel's G3 replay needs no recorded physics observations for crewmates — the Controller/Body pair is deterministic by construction. Body sets `previous := current` in `post_restore` and preserves `sub`, which resets only on the first octant change (registry `move_octant_reset`, `body_state_block`) (pipeline C5). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)* *Why normalised diagonals:* an un-normalised run diagonal (3·√2 = 4.24 px/tick = 254 px/s) would exceed the camera's pan ceiling and cut on every diagonal sprint, and it is the classic diagonal-sprint exploit. *Alternatives rejected:* `CharacterBody2D` (non-deterministic under G3, and the moving composite ship makes the engine's moving-platform handling the risk the systems index names); integer diagonal pairs ((1,1) is 71 % of walk, (2,2) is 141 %).
147	
148	*Acceleration, stopping, turning.* Start: `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` = 6 — a run begins at `v_walk` for 6 ticks, then `v_run` (integer-only; escape is never blocked because the body is already moving at walk speed on tick 1). Walk start is instant by default; `WALK_START_TICKS` (0–6, default **0**, D.4) is a weight lever that makes the first N ticks of a walk move at 1 px/tick, a rhythm-independent response to the "heavy, not sluggish" question *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; off until the feel protocol in Game Feel asks for it)*. Stop: `STOP_DECEL_TICKS` = 0 (range 0–3, integer steps only). Facing change: instant, mid-cycle (PC-4). Positions are integer base px at commit, so a stop is always on the pixel grid; **no tile snapping** on stop (an uncaused motion the player did not make; C-R's "never reverses unless the player did" extends to the body). No actor pushes another at MVP.
149	
150	*Run latch (toggle option).* With run as a toggle, the latch is set by a press and **auto-clears** after `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` = 30 ticks of `octant == NONE`, on channel start, and on entering any non-`gameplay` context — so a latched run never survives a stop the player did not re-decide.
151	
152	**PC-4. Facing: five drawn, three mirrored; derived from committed aim when the aim is live.** Facing is recomputed **every tick from committed state, with no easing, mid-cycle**, using a **2-quanta sector hysteresis** (2 × 1/128 turn = 5.6°) at octant boundaries. Priority order:
153	1. **Staggered / downed / dead**: facing frozen.
154	2. **Channelling**: facing held at the stored `channel_face` for the whole channel (the work loop is two-handed and tool-forward, 5.2; `channel_face` is written once by `set_channel_ref`'s `face_octant` at the `begin_*` apply, so a MIRROR client reads it and never recomputes it); the beam still follows aim from the locked chest point. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* A channel whose `channel_face` is none (ACTOR_SELF) holds `facing_prev` for its whole length. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*
155	3. **Running**: facing = movement octant regardless of aim. *Rationale:* the run cycle is a forward lean of the whole figure; a lean sideways to its motion reads as the horror's asymmetry (3.2 negation rule). The beam is engine light rotating 360° from the chest point (5.6), so a runner's light may point behind them — honest. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "and tense" claim was struck: retreating at full run with the beam on the pursuer cost only run noise, and the camera look-ahead even showed what is behind. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D6 option B, Open Question 19. **While running the camera look-ahead is weighted toward the movement direction** (the pipeline's D.7 `LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT`, cited by PC-5 "Two consumers" and D.7b; the Controller owns no second knob — *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, general rule G1*); the beam, `aim_angle`, `set_aim` and the sim are untouched, so turning your back on the pursuer costs the view of it, by presentation alone. The "and tense" claim is restored in this narrower form: the tension is the view, not a penalty. Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
156	4. **Aim-live** (mouse always; stick deflected): facing = aim octant, whether walking or stationary and **whether or not the beam is lit** — mouse players face the cursor and back-pedal. *Rationale (ux-designer, adopted):* the camera already leans into the aim regardless of beam state (pipeline C4); body and camera must agree, or a beam toggle would turn the body without turning the frame.
157	5. **Aim-idle, moving**: facing = movement octant.
158	6. **Aim-idle, stationary**: facing holds.
159	
160	Back-pedal and side-step use the single walk cycle; when `dot(move, facing) < 0` the Presenter plays the walk cycle **reversed** (zero extra frames). Back-pedal speed is full `v_walk` (`BACKPEDAL_FACTOR` = 1.0; any non-integer value breaks whole-px cadence, so a penalty, if ever wanted, is "walk only" or an integer). Mirroring: SW, W, NW are the SE, E, NE sheets x-flipped (`flip_h`); the hand point's x is negated and the tool changes hands (accepted, 5.6); the chest point barely moves (`|x| ≤ 2`). *Alternative rejected:* the earlier draft's "facing from aim only while the beam is lit" — body and camera would disagree whenever the beam is off.
161

## Detailed Design

### Core Rules

*Specialists consulted: game-designer (primary), gameplay-programmer, ux-designer; creative-director for Section B. Disagreements resolved and logged 2026-10-26.*

*Specialists consulted: game-designer (primary), gameplay-programmer (feel, kinematics, presentation contract), ux-designer (bindings, focus model, comfort, rebinding), with systems-designer (Suit thresholds) and creative-director (pillar alignment) as reviewers. Decisions logged 2026-10-26 (autonomous mode). Items tagged **→ ADR** are engine-integration choices deliberately left out of this behaviour spec. Rules are numbered `PC-n` (the kernel owns `CR-n`, the pipeline `C-n`/`PR-n`).*

**Vocabulary.** *Input Adapter*: the presentation-side object that reads devices, quantises, and **submits** commands as the local seat — kernel subscriber class `INPUT_SURFACE` (CR-10). *Controller Sim*: the simulation system that **owns** block `controller.state` (per controlled actor: move intent, gait, committed aim, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references, chest point and hand point) and runs step hook `controller.step` at divisor 1. *Avatar Presenter*: the `PRESENTATION`-class node that draws any crewmate body (local or remote) from read views; never submits. *LocomotionStep*: Body's pure integer kinematic step (PC-3). *Facing*: one of 8 octants (S, SE, E, NE, N, NW, W, SW), five drawn, three mirrored (art bible 5.6). *Raw aim*: the Adapter's local, un-quantised, per-frame aim; *committed aim*: `controller.state.aim_angle` as last applied. *Aim-live*: the aim source produced input this frame or (mouse) exists at all; *aim-idle*: a released stick. *Gait* ∈ {WALK, RUN}. *Body frame*: the ship-local frame of the body the actor is on (pipeline C2). *Channel*: a multi-tick action (cut, weld, patch) whose progress accrues in its owner's block. *Context*: the Adapter's input context ∈ {`gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`}.

**PC-1. Three parts, and the control-manifest lines that separate them.** (a) The **Input Adapter** reads devices, quantises, and submits `PLAYER`-origin commands as peer 1 acting on the entity the binding table binds to PlayerId 1 (CR-7). It writes no block, ever; it owns only local state (raw aim, last-acknowledged intents, hold timers, run latch, active device, context, pre-play tokens, menu latch and last NAV direction). It samples input for gameplay intents **in the physics callback immediately before `Kernel.step()`** (the MenuInput stream of PC-2a is sampled on render frames) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)*, so an intent submitted in frame N is frozen into tick T's P1 batch, applied in P2 and integrated by Body in P3 of the same tick — one tick of latency, never two. It never requests a Sanity, Attention or `PERCEPTION_OUT` read view: input mapping, dead-zones and aim source are HR-6 anchors and must be structurally unable to lie. (b) The **Controller Sim** registers `controller.state` (`SIM`, `persist = true`, `persist_scope = WORLD`, `scope = PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId, `repl_hint = SHARED_SUMMARY`), command types `set_move_intent` and `set_aim`, the `PLAYER`-origin command **`give_up {actor}`** (`coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`; validate: `loco_state == DOWNED` and no other bound seat that could revive (solo, MVP), else rejected `NOT_DOWNED`; apply: `death_tick := min(death_tick, T)`, so the existing D.14 check order does the rest in the same tick's `controller.step`: cap first, then death; PC-9) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D7, the solo "give up and reload" action)*, and hook `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`). It writes its block in its own `apply` handlers, inside its hooks, and through four published **Class B mutators** that other owners' `apply` handlers and hooks call for cross-block writes (CR-9 a): `set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)`, `clear_channel_ref(actor)`, `set_carry_ref(actor, item_id)`, `clear_carry_ref(actor)` (Interaction IA-36; Modular Ship Assembly calls `set_channel_ref(actor, ASSEMBLY, channel_id, face_octant)` and `clear_carry_ref(actor)`; `face_octant` is the owner's `octant_of(target anchor − foot)` computed at the `begin_*` apply and stored as `controller.state.channel_face`, so the facing lock of PC-4 rule 2 reads stored data that a MIRROR client has and never recomputes) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review: `face_octant` added; the mutators are not kernel-invoked callables, they take the shared `WriteScope`, report with `scope.fault` and return a status that callers propagate, while every Controller callable the kernel invokes — `validate`, `apply`, `controller.step`, `controller.noise`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `read_view` — receives `ctx` and ends in `return ctx.complete()`, kernel CR-19, delegated ruling R3)*; it may not submit `PLAYER`-origin commands (CR-3). `face_octant` ∈ {0..7, NONE}, NONE being 8, the same sentinel as `octant`. The owner passes NONE (1) for object class `ACTOR_SELF` (the self-patch has no target anchor) and (2) when `anchor_o − foot` = (0, 0); `anchor_o` is the target subject's interaction anchor (D.9) and `foot` is the actor's `pos_curr`, both in the actor's body frame, the same pair `in_reach` uses, and the octant is `octant_of` (D.8). A value outside 0..8 is `scope.fault` with a non-OK status and writes nothing. Callers: Interaction's `begin_*` applies (IA-14) and Assembly's `begin_weld` / `begin_seam_cut` applies (MSA-30). The four mutators are published here and the siblings conform. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))* It also registers the `SYSTEM`-origin command type **`stagger {actor}`** (`allowed_origins {SYSTEM}`, `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, no player binding; rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD`; `Applied` in `STAGGERED` without extending the lock, so a stagger never chains into a stun-lock), which Suit & Equipment submits on a two-band pressure drop within `STAGGER_WINDOW_TICKS` (SE-35) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from suit-and-equipment)* (Horror Entities submits none, HE-6; PC-9), and a second divisor-1 hook **`controller.noise`** (`after: [body.integrate]`, D.13). Its `SIM` read view publishes `octant`, `run`, `gait_effective`, `aim_angle`, `aim_live`, `facing`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP; user ruling X3, delegated ruling R5)*, `channel_ref`, the chest point and the hand point; `loco_state` is the name Attention (AT-31: the living-player and `IN_POD` tests) and Horror (HE-33, C-HE-18) read. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system, modular-ship-assembly, suit-and-equipment, ship-body-and-interior-physics, attention-system, horror-entities)* (c) The **Avatar Presenter** reads `body.state` (integer position prev/curr, odometer), `controller.state` (facing, gait, locomotion state, chest point, hand point), `emitter.state` (beam lit, shape) and `tick_alpha`; for the *local* avatar only it also reads the Adapter's raw aim. It writes exactly: frame index, `flip_h`, integer position, overlay visibility, light position and light rotation — **never scale, rotation, skew or modulate on the body** (lint). *Rationale.* "Controller submits via `INPUT_SURFACE` only; never writes blocks" is true of the Adapter and false of the Controller Sim; one name for both would read as "this system has no block", and facing and gait would end up as presentation state that co-op cannot replicate and a save cannot restore. *Alternative rejected:* folding the Controller Sim into Ship Body — intent and facing are seat semantics (what the player asked for, read by Interaction, Attention and the HUD); position is a kinematic fact. Keeping them apart keeps the input record separate from the integrator.

**PC-2. Input model: contexts, actions, intents, commands.** The game reads **named actions** (`StringName`, rebindable), never raw keys and never `device == 0` (4.7: `InputEvent.DEVICE_ID_MOUSE` / `DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`; identify devices by event type). **→ ADR** (InputMap vs a custom binding layer; edge detection by event vs polling).

*Contexts.* Exactly one context is active: `gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`. Entering any non-`gameplay` context sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and clears the run latch; entering `chart_table` or `chat` also submits `cancel_channel` for a hold- **or** toggle-mode channel (in the co-op overlay the sim keeps running and a channel the player cannot see must not keep burning); entering `inspect_card` does **not** cancel the channel, so the Pillar 4 "second instrument" check on the pipe being welded is free (the zeroed move intent is not a move, the channel continues, `interact` is still tracked for hold mode and a release inside the card still cancels; `cancel` closes the card first and a second `cancel` cancels the channel). **Movement closes the card** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D94, the Controller's context-matrix amendment adopted; the In-World Instruments fallback "buffer and replay the first move press" is void)*: a **fresh** movement input in `inspect_card` (a `move_*` key going down, or the left stick crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`) returns the context to `gameplay` **and** submits `set_move_intent` for that octant in the same frame, in that order, so the first press both closes the card and moves the avatar (nothing is swallowed, nothing is buffered). A direction already held when the card opened is latched and does not count until it is released (or the stick falls below the exit band) and pressed again, so opening the card while walking does not close it on the next frame. A move that closes the card while a channel is running is an ordinary non-`NONE` move intent and aborts the channel exactly as it does in `gameplay`. Any transition of `loco_state` to `STAGGERED`, `DOWNED`, `DEAD` or `IN_POD` returns the context to `gameplay` on the same frame (the Adapter observes the published state; the card or overlay closes and the cursor is hidden again). Pause is reachable in every state including `DOWNED`: `chart_table` and `request_pause` are Adapter-level and never gated by `loco_state`. The full **context × action matrix** is in the table below. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; supersedes the earlier "cancel all channels on every non-`gameplay` entry" note for `inspect_card` only. *Default bindings (`chart_table` context).* No new action. The Adapter (never the Chart Table) reads the physical controls of `move_up/down/left/right` (WASD, left stick) plus the arrow keys and the d-pad, four-way under `MOVE_DEADZONE` / `MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`; accept is the physical controls of `interact` in this context minus every mouse button (E, gamepad A), plus Enter and Space as fixed additional keyboard accept bindings of this context; back is `cancel` (X / B); close is `chart_table` (Esc / Start); every mouse button and the wheel are `POINTER` events only, never an accept. Conflicts are checked per context (PC-13). The gameplay-context `interact` alias LMB (default bindings table) is unchanged. All of it reaches the layer as the MenuInput stream (PC-2a). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)* **Console seam:** at the pod console the Adapter injects the host-local `ChartPick` into `pod_hop`'s payload; a console press with no pick submits nothing and opens the chart (`chart_table` context) instead — a context switch, not a verb choice (Chart Table ASK-CT-1, ASK-CT-2). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus)*

**PC-2a. MenuInput stream (Adapter-owned; consumer: the Chart Table layer, CT-45).** *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6; answers Chart Table ASK-CT-15)* The Adapter publishes a presentation-local MenuInput event stream while the active context is `chart_table`; before a campaign is loaded (the boot-flow screens) the Adapter runs in the `chart_table` context with no gameplay sink and publishes the same stream. It is sampled on render frames (the physics-callback sampling of PC-1 (a) serves gameplay intents only); all events of one render frame are delivered in arrival order at the start of that frame, before the layer's update. **Events:** `NAV_DOWN{dir, source}` and `NAV_UP{dir}` (`dir` ∈ {UP, DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT}; `source` ∈ {STICK, DPAD, ARROW, WASD}); `ACCEPT_DOWN`, `ACCEPT_UP`; `BACK`; `CLOSE`; `FOCUS_OUT`, `FOCUS_IN`; `DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`; `POINTER{kind ∈ {MOVE, DOWN, UP, WHEEL}, button, position}`, where `position` is the cursor relative to the picture rectangle's origin, which is `cursor_vp` itself (the D.7 variable table measures `cursor_vp` from the world picture's origin, so nothing is subtracted twice), in the unit of `cursor_vp` (D.7 variable table; the unit under the `canvas_items` stretch is **[UNV]** until the spike of Chart Table AC-CT-135 (f) reads it). **The Adapter owns:** (a) **echo suppression**: an OS key echo of a held E, Enter, Space, Esc or X produces no second event (the engine's echo flag is **[UNV]** until the ADR spike); (b) **deadzone hysteresis**: a stick takes a NAV edge on crossing `MOVE_DEADZONE` from below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT` and releases below `MOVE_DEADZONE − MOVE_DEADZONE_EXIT`, the same band as the `inspect_card` movement rule (PC-2 contexts); (c) **the cardinal-axis rule**: a stick yields one NAV direction at a time, the axis with the larger magnitude, a tie going to the vertical axis; the taken direction changes only after the stick has re-passed the exit band, so a diagonal drift cannot alternate; auto-repeat of a held NAV direction is the layer's (Chart Table D.9); (d) **latch-until-released**: for any physical control whose press closed the layer (Resume accept, `chart_table`, `cancel`) the Adapter emits nothing from that control, to the layer or to gameplay, until it is physically released and pressed again, including across the `PAUSED → RUNNING` resync (Edge Cases, kernel `PAUSED`); for a console press that opened the layer, the open press's release and repeats are latched the same way; (e) **focus**: `FOCUS_OUT` releases every held menu control and clears navigation state, and the layer's hold fills abort; on `FOCUS_IN` nothing is held and fresh presses are required; (f) **`DEVICE_CHANGED{device}`** is published when the last-used-device glyph set changes under PC-13 (immediately, except inside `DEVICE_SWITCH_HYSTERESIS` of the previous change, when it is published at the window end), so the layer adds no delay; (g) **the cursor hint**: the layer publishes `cursor_hint` ∈ {DEFAULT, SELECTABLE}; the Adapter, its only `Input` caller, applies the pointer-cursor shape. The `zoom_*` edges are never emitted in this context (PC-16). The stream carries no gameplay command and no simulation read. Its code lives in the Adapter's registered files (AC-PCI-176).

*Dev-only actions (dev feature tag only).* The Adapter registers the ten actions of registry `debug_overlay_actions` — `debug_overlay_toggle`, `debug_overlay_page_next`, `debug_overlay_page_prev`, `debug_overlay_mode`, `debug_overlay_dump`, `debug_overlay_reveal`, `debug_overlay_mark`, `debug_overlay_cursor_next`, `debug_overlay_cursor_prev`, `debug_overlay_activate` (placeholder defaults toggle F3, page next F4, page prev Shift+F4, mode Insert, dump Home, reveal Ctrl+Shift+F3 with the pad chord L3 + R3, mark End, cursor next PageDown, cursor prev PageUp, activate Delete; F5-F8 avoided as editor run, pause and stop shortcuts; Debug Overlay DO-8) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* — **only under the dev feature tag**, and forwards them host-locally to the Overlay: never a command, never in the binding table Settings sees, never in a rebinding, preset or accessibility enumeration, absent from release. The Adapter is their only `Input` reader (Gaps: the cross-GDD lint collision). **Pad chord:** the dev chord L3 + R3 shadows no gameplay action now that `throw` is on RB; L3 and R3 are unbound by default in every build. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from debug-overlay-true-values; rewritten 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "R3 consumed by the chord before `throw`" rule is void)*

*Intents vs commands (CR-4).* Two types are **intents**, `coalesce = LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`, `max_age_ticks = 30`: **`set_move_intent {octant: 0..7 | 8 = NONE, run: bool}`** and **`set_aim {aim_angle: int, live: bool}`** in **1/4096-turn units** (`live` is `aim_live`: it travels with the angle because facing rules 4–6 branch on it in the sim). Both intents carry `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER` with `actor_source = body.state` (the avatar's Body `actor_id`, kernel CR-7), like commands. Everything else is a **command**: `coalesce = NONE`, `max_age_ticks = 120`, `actor_binding = OWNED_BY_ISSUER`, `actor_source` as its owner declares (`body.state` for every avatar-acting verb; `emitter.state` for `toggle_beam`, whose `actor` is the seat's beam id) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. The Adapter sends `set_move_intent` **only on change** of octant or `run`, with the stick quantised to 8 octants under `MOVE_DEADZONE` = 0.25 and `OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG` = 5°. In one frame it submits `set_move_intent` **before** any command (submission order is the P2 apply order — the kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source) from it, and callers never choose it, delegated ruling R2 — so a stop and a `begin_*` in the same frame apply in that order, PC-7). It sends `set_aim` when the quantised value differs from `last_acked` by **≥ 1/128 turn (2.8°)**, **or** the aim source changed (mouse ↔ stick ↔ keys), **or** `live` changed, **or** a settle condition holds (inside the threshold but differing at all, for `AIM_SETTLE_TICKS` = 6) — **rate-limited to one per `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL` = 3 ticks**. At rest that is zero sends; a sweep is ≤ 20 sends/s, far inside `MAX_CMDS_PER_TICK`. **No input buffering**: `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS` = 0; a press during a channel is submitted and answered `BUSY`, honestly; nothing is queued for "after". *Rationale:* buffering hides the sim's answer behind a presentation guess; Zomboid's immediacy is the model. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Zero buffering is a recorded, deliberate trade, not an oversight:** an `interact` for a `CHANNEL` verb pressed one to three ticks before the move keys are up is rejected `MOVING` (PC-7) and costs one honest re-press; the same-tick case (release W and press E in one frame) is solved by ordering, not by buffering (intents are submitted first and validation reads `intent_octant`, PC-7). Adapter-side lever, **off at MVP**: `CHANNEL_BEGIN_GRACE_TICKS` (0–3, default **0**) would hold a `begin_*` press until the Adapter's own last-submitted octant is NONE for at most that many ticks; a playtest finding of "my weld never starts" is the trigger to raise it. *Ignored-input cues (accessibility):* four presses are dropped by Adapter-local knowledge alone and play one short dull cue (`cue_input_ignored`, the same id for all four, no visual, never read from a sim result): `toggle_beam` inside the rate-limit window (PC-5), `interact` with no focused object, `run` while `carry_ref ≠ none`, and `run` while the player's own inventory view shows a HEAVY item stowed (`stowed_heavy`, user ruling D18 and D.4; the name is the one Suit & Equipment publishes, registry `stowed_heavy`, and the earlier `heavy_stowed` is retired *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, general rule G1)*; it is the consequence of the player's own stow command, not a hidden reading) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings: D18)*. The cue is Adapter-local and so cannot reveal a sim answer; `run` under Suit's cap gets none (the cap is Suit's state, shown by the breath and warmth readings).

*Immediate acknowledgement and the pre-play token (CR-4).* On submit the Adapter pre-plays **body and sound only, never the effect**: the hand's switch animation, the tool click, the bar starting. Each pre-play is keyed by an opaque integer **`correlation`** the Adapter attaches to the command (a per-Adapter counter; the kernel echoes it unchanged in the result or rejection event; `submit()` stays void and fire-and-forget, and the kernel, not the caller, stamps `seq`) in a `correlation → pre-play token` map, so a late result cancels the right pre-play *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R2)*. The beam light is the one object that is not pre-played (PC-5). **Rejection classes** (declared by each verb's owner, Interaction's GDD): *immediate* reasons — `OUT_OF_RANGE`, `BUSY`, `INVALID_TARGET`, `ACTOR_NOT_OWNED`, `PAUSED`, every admission reason — **withdraw the ack at once** (the sound stops, the bar vanishes within one frame of the result); the free-lie-detector case of Pillar 4 (a device the player perceives as broken or fixed) is **not a rejection**: the command is `Applied` and the channel resolves to a `PRECONDITION` outcome (Interaction, KRN:96), so the ack is never withdrawn — the work loop and the bar continue until Interaction's channel state signals the outcome. **The ack frame for a command whose channel will complete and one whose channel will resolve to `PRECONDITION` must be pixel- and sound-identical.** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from interaction-system)* Rejection is never a shake (C9, HR-13).

*Non-audio counterpart (HUD-owned; reduced to the MOVING tell).* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated CD ruling, HUD re-review K43)* Every negative cue was audio-only, so deaf and hard-of-hearing players got none, and nothing taught the three core rules (channels need stillness, prompts need light, destructive verbs need a hold). The only non-audio counterpart at MVP is the pre-press tell for a `begin_*` press that the actor's **own** state would block (`MOVING`): Interaction's `focus_view.press_blocked_moving`, drawn by HUD as a hollow keycap on `CHANNEL` and `HOLD_CONFIRM` plates (Interaction IA-41, AC-IA-142). The Adapter publishes **no** `input_ignored_view(seat)` and no reason class to the HUD: a visible response to a `NOT_LIT` (or any subject-dependent) press would tell the player something is at the unlit subject, the unlit-subject oracle Pillar 3 forbids, so the glyph dim on `NOT_LIT`, `BUSY`-by-other-seat, `OUT_OF_RANGE` and `INVALID_TARGET` presses is refused; the HUD still holds the restored keycap for `BAR_REJECT_HOLD_TICKS` on a plate Interaction has already shown (HUD HS-41). The other ignored-input cues (`cue_input_ignored`: `toggle_beam` in its window, `interact` with no focus, `run` while carrying) stay audio-only at MVP; a non-audio counterpart for them is deferred to `design/accessibility-requirements.md` (Open Question 26) and must not key on subject existence or lighting. **First-use hints are refused**: no caption, no Settings "seen" flag, no "reset profile" interaction (HUD HS-57, anti-pillar 4; teaching belongs to the world, Cryo Bay onboarding). **Playtest metric:** ≥ 80 % of first-time testers complete the first weld within two attempts; a miss reopens the Cryo Bay onboarding (HUD OQ-HS-29), not the rules and not a HUD hint.

*Resync rule (one rule, five triggers).* The Adapter keeps `last_acked` per intent type and must **resend its current quantised value, bypassing the change filter once**, when: (i) an intent result arrives `Rejected(STALE)` (kernel Edge Cases: a stale "stop" otherwise leaves the actor moving); (ii) the kernel leaves `PAUSED` (CR-16 rejects intents immediately while paused, so a release during a pause was lost); (iii) `LOADING → RUNNING`; (iv) window focus returns, or the active gamepad reconnects; (v) **`TRANSFER`**: the actor's `body_of_actor` changes, i.e. a pod arrival (`IN_POD →` the locomotion-class member) or a section-detach body transfer, because the new body's first tick must act on the keys physically held *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: pod arrival and body transfer were handled only as an ad-hoc "treated as trigger iii" in Edge Cases)*. For a hold-mode channel it compares the actual button state to the last submitted one on each of those and submits `cancel_channel` if the button is up. **Window focus loss** submits `set_move_intent {NONE}` and `cancel_channel` if channelling, and marks every held action released; **the loss of the active gamepad** (a disconnect, mid-weld included) is treated identically (the same zero intent and cancel, the held pad actions released, the keyboard and mouse stay live, and a reconnect resyncs under trigger iv), and **the click or key press that returns window focus is consumed by the Adapter** and never reaches a binding (an LMB alias of `interact` would otherwise fire on refocus) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Invariant (testable): the sim's intent equals the player's hands within one tick of the kernel being `RUNNING`.

**PC-3. Movement: ship-local, 8-way, two gaits, whole base pixels per tick, no physics body.** Movement is in the **body frame** (pipeline C2); the interior never shows ship motion. Input is **8-way**; gait is the `run` action, never stick deflection. *Rationale:* the noise cost of running (PC-10) must be a deliberate input, not a thumb slip (Sirlin's test for a real decision), and analog speed would be a continuum of non-integer px/tick, which PR-4 rule 3 forbids at camera quantum 1.

*Speeds — derivation.* The pipeline routes "whole base px per tick when the quantum is 1" (PR-4 rule 3) and asserts two build invariants on `v_max`: `LAG_CUT > v_max·τ_follow` → `v_max < 266 px/s`, **and** `0.30·L_h > v_max·τ_follow + L_MAX` at the default field → `0.18·v_max + 72 ≤ 108` → **`v_max < 200 px/s`**. The second binds (the gameplay-programmer's reading and the game-designer's coincide); the brief's 266 is not the operative bound. At `TICK_RATE` = 60 the whole-px/tick ladder is 60 / 120 / 180 / 240 px/s, so the integer ceiling is **3 px/tick = 180 px/s** (lag 32.4 px; 32.4 + 72 = 104.4 ≤ 108). The pipeline's placeholders 90 / 150 px/s are 1.5 / 2.5 px/tick — non-integer under its own routed rule — and are superseded (routed correction).

| Knob | Value | px/s at 60 Hz | tiles/s | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `v_walk` (registry: `V_WALK`) | **2 px/tick** | 120 | 2.5 | Deliberate but not tedious: the 13-tile default field crosses in ≈ 5 s; the boarding rhythm's pace is set by doors and reading. 1 px/tick recorded as the playtest alternative |
| `v_run` (registry: `V_RUN`) | **3 px/tick** | 180 | 3.75 | The integer ceiling under the inner-box invariant; 1.5× walk reads with the forward lean (5.2) and never clamps the camera |
| `v_carry` (registry: `V_CARRY`) | **1 px/tick** | 60 | 1.25 | A module at chest height halves the walk; extraction under rising Attention is the sortie's tension, and the slowdown is *seen* (carry-walk cycle), never a hidden stat |
| `v_max` | = `v_run` | 180 | — | Read by the pipeline's G check |

All speeds are in px/tick and are invalidated by a `TICK_RATE` change (kernel Open Question 12).

*Kinematics (Body's mechanism, this GDD's contract — Body to confirm).* **The avatar has no physics body.** Ship Body runs a hand-rolled integer kinematic step `LocomotionStep.step(state, intent, collide: Callable)` — a pure `RefCounted`, headless-testable: `pos: Vector2i` (base px, body frame) plus `sub: Vector2i` in **1/256-px fixed point**; velocity from an 8-entry integer unit table (cardinal 256, **diagonal 181/256** per axis, so diagonal speed equals cardinal speed to 0.1 %); **axis-separated 1-px AABB sweeps**, x then y every tick, against Layout's integer footprint rectangles, consumed as `SIMULATION` data (walls 24 px deep under the up-screen convention, closed door leaves, props, machinery) — sliding along a wall falls out of axis separation; `sub` **resets to zero on stop**; the foot box is **16 × 8 base px**, horizontally centred on the foot origin, which is the box's top row (`[pos.x − 8, pos.x + 8) × [pos.y, pos.y + 8)`; registry `foot_box`, `FOOT_BOX_W`, `FOOT_BOX_H`). Consequence: the avatar's position is a **pure function of the command stream and the layout**, so the kernel's G3 replay needs no recorded physics observations for crewmates — the Controller/Body pair is deterministic by construction. Body sets `previous := current` in `post_restore` and preserves `sub`, which resets only on the first octant change (registry `move_octant_reset`, `body_state_block`) (pipeline C5). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)* *Why normalised diagonals:* an un-normalised run diagonal (3·√2 = 4.24 px/tick = 254 px/s) would exceed the camera's pan ceiling and cut on every diagonal sprint, and it is the classic diagonal-sprint exploit. *Alternatives rejected:* `CharacterBody2D` (non-deterministic under G3, and the moving composite ship makes the engine's moving-platform handling the risk the systems index names); integer diagonal pairs ((1,1) is 71 % of walk, (2,2) is 141 %).

*Acceleration, stopping, turning.* Start: `RUN_RAMP_TICKS` = 6 — a run begins at `v_walk` for 6 ticks, then `v_run` (integer-only; escape is never blocked because the body is already moving at walk speed on tick 1). Walk start is instant by default; `WALK_START_TICKS` (0–6, default **0**, D.4) is a weight lever that makes the first N ticks of a walk move at 1 px/tick, a rhythm-independent response to the "heavy, not sluggish" question *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; off until the feel protocol in Game Feel asks for it)*. Stop: `STOP_DECEL_TICKS` = 0 (range 0–3, integer steps only). Facing change: instant, mid-cycle (PC-4). Positions are integer base px at commit, so a stop is always on the pixel grid; **no tile snapping** on stop (an uncaused motion the player did not make; C-R's "never reverses unless the player did" extends to the body). No actor pushes another at MVP.

*Run latch (toggle option).* With run as a toggle, the latch is set by a press and **auto-clears** after `RUN_LATCH_CLEAR` = 30 ticks of `octant == NONE`, on channel start, and on entering any non-`gameplay` context — so a latched run never survives a stop the player did not re-decide.

**PC-4. Facing: five drawn, three mirrored; derived from committed aim when the aim is live.** Facing is recomputed **every tick from committed state, with no easing, mid-cycle**, using a **2-quanta sector hysteresis** (2 × 1/128 turn = 5.6°) at octant boundaries. Priority order:
1. **Staggered / downed / dead**: facing frozen.
2. **Channelling**: facing held at the stored `channel_face` for the whole channel (the work loop is two-handed and tool-forward, 5.2; `channel_face` is written once by `set_channel_ref`'s `face_octant` at the `begin_*` apply, so a MIRROR client reads it and never recomputes it); the beam still follows aim from the locked chest point. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* A channel whose `channel_face` is none (ACTOR_SELF) holds `facing_prev` for its whole length. *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*
3. **Running**: facing = movement octant regardless of aim. *Rationale:* the run cycle is a forward lean of the whole figure; a lean sideways to its motion reads as the horror's asymmetry (3.2 negation rule). The beam is engine light rotating 360° from the chest point (5.6), so a runner's light may point behind them — honest. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review: the earlier "and tense" claim was struck: retreating at full run with the beam on the pursuer cost only run noise, and the camera look-ahead even showed what is behind. Resolved 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions): D6 option B, Open Question 19. **While running the camera look-ahead is weighted toward the movement direction** (the pipeline's D.7 `LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT`, cited by PC-5 "Two consumers" and D.7b; the Controller owns no second knob — *Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, general rule G1*); the beam, `aim_angle`, `set_aim` and the sim are untouched, so turning your back on the pursuer costs the view of it, by presentation alone. The "and tense" claim is restored in this narrower form: the tension is the view, not a penalty. Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
4. **Aim-live** (mouse always; stick deflected): facing = aim octant, whether walking or stationary and **whether or not the beam is lit** — mouse players face the cursor and back-pedal. *Rationale (ux-designer, adopted):* the camera already leans into the aim regardless of beam state (pipeline C4); body and camera must agree, or a beam toggle would turn the body without turning the frame.
5. **Aim-idle, moving**: facing = movement octant.
6. **Aim-idle, stationary**: facing holds.

Back-pedal and side-step use the single walk cycle; when `dot(move, facing) < 0` the Presenter plays the walk cycle **reversed** (zero extra frames). Back-pedal speed is full `v_walk` (`BACKPEDAL_FACTOR` = 1.0; any non-integer value breaks whole-px cadence, so a penalty, if ever wanted, is "walk only" or an integer). Mirroring: SW, W, NW are the SE, E, NE sheets x-flipped (`flip_h`); the hand point's x is negated and the tool changes hands (accepted, 5.6); the chest point barely moves (`|x| ≤ 2`). *Alternative rejected:* the earlier draft's "facing from aim only while the beam is lit" — body and camera would disagree whenever the beam is off.

Position ownership — adopted (kernel Open Question 3 / pipeline Open Question 3 closed against Ship Body; technical-director ratification pending).** **Adopted: Ship Body owns ship-local integer position (`pos`, `sub`, `odometer`, `LocomotionStep`); the Controller Sim owns intent, gait, committed aim, facing, locomotion state, carry and channel references, chest point and hand point.** Contract: `controller.step` writes `octant`, `gait_effective`, `facing`, `loco_state`; `body.integrate` (divisor 1, `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model)* runs `LocomotionStep` with `collide` bound to Layout's integer footprint rectangles (`SIMULATION` data) and commits `pos_prev / pos_curr`, `odometer`, `blocked`. *Why Body:* the composite welded ship is Body's (systems index high-risk row); an actor transfers between bodies (pod hop, detach) which Body tracks; and with no physics body the step is deterministic, so G3 needs no physics observations for crewmates. *Why not Controller:* it would put the Layout projection inside an input system. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Adopted by Ship Body & Interior Physics** (designed: its "Who owns what" section, BDY-7, BDY-9, BDY-10 take this split verbatim, and the foot box 16 × 8, the 1/256 fixed point and `trunc` rounding are Body's confirmed values); only the technical-director's ratification in the weld spike remains. Body's persisted `last_octant` (the octant its last step integrated) is a different field from this block's `last_octant` (the D.5 decel-ladder memory); both names are kept and the distinction is stated in PC-17.

**PC-15. Hook order and timing.** `controller.step` (divisor 1, `after: suit.vitals`) → `body.integrate` (divisor 1, `after: [controller.step, layout.doors]`; owner Ship Body, BDY-8) → `controller.noise` (divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate]`; reads Body's derived `moved(actor_id)` and pushes the gait class, D.13) and `emitter.place` (divisor 1, `after: [body.integrate, graph.propagate.failure]`; beam emitter at the chest point for the exposure query) → Attention (divisor 6) integrates the pushed noise; a push landing after `attention.step` in a tick integrates on its next run (registry `push_stimulus`; Attention may add `controller.noise` to its own `after` list). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from ship-body-and-interior-physics, ship-section-and-layout-data-model, emitter-state-and-light-exposure-query, attention-system)* Input-to-effect: sampled before `Kernel.step()`, applied P2, integrated P3, drawn next render (≤ 17 ms + render latency).

**PC-16. Inputs owned here, consumed elsewhere.** `zoom_in` / `zoom_out` are two edge-triggered player inputs (pipeline C1) consumed by the pipeline's zoom ladder; `chart_table` calls `request_pause` (CR-15) through the menu in single-player and opens an overlay with the kernel `RUNNING` in co-op (CR-16); `inspect` enters the `inspect_card` context (the Adapter is the `INPUT_SURFACE` and owns the context; it publishes a presentation-local `{context, inspect_ref}` signal that In-World Instruments, a `PRESENTATION` surface, subscribe to — registry `inspect_card_context_signal`; never a command). The inspect card ships live at MVP (In-World Instruments IW-21). In `inspect_card`, `set_aim` stays live (the Adapter keeps sampling aim and sending `set_aim` as in `gameplay`), so the lamp can hold the gauge lit; the OS cursor stays hidden there (HUD HS-52; the mouse still steers the aim and picks nothing on the card, Instruments K-14) *(corrected 2026-10-27 — design review)*. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from in-world-instruments-and-inspect-view)* In `PAUSED` the Adapter submits no intents and resyncs on resume (PC-2).

**PC-17. Save, restore and co-op seams.** `controller.state` persists (`WORLD`). **The rest normalisation lives in `snapshot()`, not in `restore()`:** `snapshot()` writes the transient input fields at their rest values — `octant = NONE`, `run = false`, `channel_ref = none`, `channel_face = none` (so `face_octant` is never recomputed after a restore) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6/G1, blocker PC-1(b))*, `loco_state` as live except that `WALK`, `RUN`, `CARRY_WALK`, `CHANNELLING` and `STAGGERED` are written as `IDLE` (stagger timer cleared), so a persisted `octant == NONE` never sits beside a moving `loco_state` that Attention and Horror read as the class invariant, and the first `controller.step` after the restore recomputes the class member from the resynced intent by the step order of States and Transitions; `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix; delegated ruling G6, GAP; user ruling X3, delegated ruling R5)*, `facing`, `aim_angle` and `aim_live` as live *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* — and `restore()` is a whole-block replace that normalises nothing, so `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is byte-identical in canonical bytes (kernel K:839, CR-8; Save/Load SL-15 item 10) and a loaded game still never resumes mid-move, mid-channel or mid-stagger. Integer vectors persist as two ints or a packed int array, never `Vector2i` (SL-2). This answers Save/Load OQ-9: `controller.state` is not in `REBASE_BLOCKS` (Save/Load's list, registry value `[interaction.state, assembly.state]`: `controller.state` and `body.state` are not listed, because the Controller normalises in `snapshot()` and BDY-31 makes Body's block restore-idempotent at block level); restore verification of this block is `EXACT`. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* A restore restarts the run ramp (the resync re-sends `run`), so G4 fixtures walk across the snapshot tick. Body sets `previous := current` in `post_restore` and preserves `sub` (it resets on the first octant change, registry `move_octant_reset`) (pipeline C5). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format, ship-body-and-interior-physics)* VS-B: a guest's Adapter submits identically and the host's Controller Sim applies; `controller.state` and `body.state` replicate as `SHARED_SUMMARY`; remote crewmates' beams rotate from the **replicated committed aim, which may not be coarsened below the facing hysteresis** (1/64 turn) so facing agrees on every client; **no shared or assisted control** of any kind; the player's **own identity glyph** (beam shape + band count) sits on the suit panel; crewmate names are **press-to-reveal for ≈ 2 s and lit-only**; pings (if adopted) mark lit things only. Nothing in the Presenter branches on `HOST` / `MIRROR` (CR-10).

# TRs: Player Controller & Input (pc)

Source: design/gdd/player-controller-input.md

| Req ID | Requirement | Domain | GDD anchor |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-pc-001 | The system is split into three parts: Input Adapter (presentation, submits PLAYER-origin commands as peer 1, writes no block), Controller Sim (owns `controller.state`), Avatar Presenter (PRESENTATION, never submits); a lint verifies the Adapter writes no block. | Core | PC-1 |
| TR-pc-002 | `controller.state` is registered as SIM, `persist=true`, `persist_scope=WORLD`, `scope=PER_PLAYER` keyed by PlayerId, `repl_hint=SHARED_SUMMARY`, holding intent, gait, committed aim, facing, loco_state, carry/channel refs, channel_face, chest point and hand point. | Core | PC-1(b), PC-14 |
| TR-pc-003 | Ship Body owns ship-local integer position (`pos`, `sub`, `odometer`, `LocomotionStep`); Controller Sim owns intent/gait/aim/facing/loco_state/carry/channel (PC-14, pending TD ratification). | Core | PC-14 |
| TR-pc-004 | The Adapter samples gameplay intents in the physics callback immediately before `Kernel.step()` so an intent submitted in frame N is applied in P2 and integrated in P3 of the same tick (one tick latency, never two). | Threading/Timing | PC-1(a), PC-15 |
| TR-pc-005 | Hook order is `suit.vitals` -> `controller.step` (divisor 1) -> `layout.doors` -> `body.integrate` -> `controller.noise` and `emitter.place`; Attention (divisor 6) integrates pushed noise; the order is asserted from the hook registry. | Threading/Timing | PC-15, AC-PCI-209 |
| TR-pc-006 | `set_move_intent {octant 0..7\|8=NONE, run}` and `set_aim {aim_angle int 1/4096 turn, live}` are intents with `coalesce=LATEST_PER_ACTOR_PER_TICK`, `max_age_ticks=30`; all other commands use `coalesce=NONE`, `max_age_ticks=120`; all use `actor_binding=OWNED_BY_ISSUER` with `actor_source`. | Core | PC-2 intents vs commands |
| TR-pc-007 | The Adapter sends `set_move_intent` only on change (8 octants, `MOVE_DEADZONE`=0.25, `OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG`=5), submits it before any command in the same frame, and sends `set_aim` at most once per `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL`=3 ticks (<=26 commands/s total). | Input | PC-2, AC-PCI-221 |
| TR-pc-008 | No input buffering: `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS`=0; a press during a channel is submitted and answered honestly (`BUSY`/`MOVING`), nothing is queued. | Input | PC-2 |
| TR-pc-009 | The Adapter keeps `last_acked` per intent and resends its current value once, bypassing the change filter, on the five resync triggers (STALE reject, leaving PAUSED, LOADING->RUNNING, focus/gamepad return, body TRANSFER); focus or gamepad loss sends `set_move_intent {NONE}` and `cancel_channel`. | Input | PC-2 Resync rule |
| TR-pc-010 | Exactly one input context is active (`gameplay`, `chart_table`, `inspect_card`, `chat`); the context x action matrix governs which actions are live, and STAGGERED/DOWNED/DEAD/IN_POD force a return to `gameplay`; `chart_table` entry and `chat` entry cancel channels, `inspect_card` does not. | Input | PC-2 context matrix |
| TR-pc-011 | Game code reads named rebindable actions (StringName), never raw keys or `device == 0`; devices are identified by event type; per-context conflict checking applies. | Input | PC-2, PC-13 |
| TR-pc-012 | The Adapter publishes a presentation-local MenuInput event stream (NAV_DOWN/UP, ACCEPT, BACK, CLOSE, FOCUS_IN/OUT, DEVICE_CHANGED, POINTER) sampled on render frames with echo suppression, deadzone hysteresis, cardinal-axis rule and latch-until-released. | UI | PC-2a |
| TR-pc-013 | Movement is hand-rolled integer kinematics (`LocomotionStep`, pure RefCounted, 1/256-px fixed point, axis-separated 1-px AABB sweeps, diagonal 181/256) with no physics body and no CharacterBody2D; avatar position is a pure function of command stream and layout (deterministic for replay G3/G4). | Physics | PC-3 |
| TR-pc-014 | Speeds are whole base px per tick: `v_walk`=2, `v_run`=3, `v_carry`=1; `v_max`=`v_run` must satisfy build invariants I1 (`LAG_CUT` > v_max*tau) and I2 (`v_run*TICK_RATE*FOLLOW_TAU + L_MAX <= 0.30*field_h`); the loader refuses data violating any of the 19 invariants, naming exactly the violated set. | Data | PC-3, Tuning Knobs invariants, AC-PCI-200..203 |
| TR-pc-015 | Tick-expressed knobs (units `ticks` or `px/tick`) are invalidated by a `TICK_RATE` change, detected data-driven from the unit column. | Data | PC-3, AC-PCI-212 |
| TR-pc-016 | Facing is recomputed every tick from committed state with a 2-quanta (1/128 turn) hysteresis and the six-level priority order (frozen / channel_face / running / aim-live / aim-idle moving / hold); a MIRROR client never recomputes facing or channel_face from aim. | Core | PC-4, AC-PCI-197 |
| TR-pc-017 | The Controller Sim publishes a SIM read view (`octant`, `run`, `gait_effective`, `aim_angle`, `aim_live`, `facing`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry`, `channel_ref`, chest point, hand point); Attention and Horror read only `loco_state` and never other Controller state. | Core | PC-1(b) |
| TR-pc-018 | Four Class B mutators (`set_channel_ref(actor, owner_system, channel_id, face_octant)`, `clear_channel_ref`, `set_carry_ref`, `clear_carry_ref`) are the only cross-block write path; they take the shared `WriteScope`, report via `scope.fault`, reject `face_octant` outside 0..8, and callers propagate the status. | Core | PC-1(b) |
| TR-pc-019 | Every kernel-invoked Controller callable (`validate`, `apply`, `controller.step`, `controller.noise`, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `read_view`) receives `ctx` and ends in `return ctx.complete()`. | Core | PC-1(b) (CR-19, R3) |
| TR-pc-020 | `snapshot()` normalises transient fields (`octant=NONE`, `run=false`, `channel_ref/channel_face=none`, moving loco_states written as IDLE) while `restore()` is a whole-block replace, so `snapshot(restore(snapshot()))` is canonical-byte identical; `controller.state` is not in `REBASE_BLOCKS` and restore verification is EXACT; integer vectors persist as ints or packed arrays, never `Vector2i`. | Save/Load | PC-17, AC-PCI-191..193 |
| TR-pc-021 | The persisted payload contains no Adapter-local state (`last_acked`, hold timers, run latch, device, context, pre-play tokens). | Save/Load | AC-PCI-192 |
| TR-pc-022 | DEAD hand-off: the death stub makes exactly one `request_restore`, honoured only after Save/Load's epoch staging reports `EPOCH_DURABLE`; `loco_state` stays DEAD with no further transition and the seat accepts no commands. | Save/Load | States DEAD, AC-PCI-199 |
| TR-pc-023 | `give_up {actor}` (PLAYER origin, `coalesce=NONE`, `max_age_ticks=120`) is valid only in DOWNED solo (else `NOT_DOWNED`) and sets `death_tick := min(death_tick, T)`; `stagger {actor}` is SYSTEM-origin only, rejected `NOT_STAGGERABLE` in DOWNED/DEAD/IN_POD, and does not extend the lock. | Core | PC-1(b), PC-9 |
| TR-pc-024 | Command authority: a command with `issuer_peer` not owning the actor is `Rejected(ACTOR_NOT_OWNED)` at P2 with no state change; no shared or assisted control exists; the Adapter attaches an opaque integer `correlation` and keys pre-play tokens by it; pre-play is body/sound only, never the effect or beam light. | Networking | PC-2, PC-17, AC-PCI-194 |
| TR-pc-025 | The Adapter never reads Sanity, Attention or PERCEPTION_OUT views (input mapping, deadzones, aim source are HR-6 anchors); the Controller's Suit read is `locomotion_cap` only; Sanity may never alter bindings, aim or movement. | Core | PC-1(a), PC-9, PC-10, AC-PCI-210 |
| TR-pc-026 | The Avatar Presenter writes only `frame`, `flip_h`, integer `position`, overlay `visible` and the Light2D `position`/`rotation`; never scale, rotation, skew, modulate or tweens on them; position is `floor(lerp(prev, curr, tick_alpha))` with zero fractional part; it contains no HOST/MIRROR branch. | Rendering | PC-1(c), AC-PCI-195, 207, 208 |
| TR-pc-027 | Controller and body sources contain no forbidden time/RNG calls (`Time.get_ticks_*`, `get_process_delta_time`, `randi`, `randf`, `RandomNumberGenerator`) except allow-listed render-time timers in Adapter/Presenter. | Threading/Timing | AC-PCI-211 |
| TR-pc-028 | Under co-op, `controller.state` and `body.state` replicate as `SHARED_SUMMARY`; the replicated `aim_angle` quantum may not exceed `FACING_HYSTERESIS` (64 units) or boot faults with `REPL_QUANTUM_TOO_COARSE{aim_angle}`. | Networking | PC-17, AC-PCI-196 |
| TR-pc-029 | Per-component CPU sub-budgets (advisory, RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK release export): Adapter <=0.1 ms/frame, `LocomotionStep` <=0.05 ms/actor/tick (2,000 rects), `controller.step` <=0.02 ms/actor/tick, Presenter <=0.1 ms/avatar/frame, diagnostics <=0.01 ms/tick. | Performance | Performance budget, AC-PCI-217..222 |
| TR-pc-030 | Dev-only artifacts (`PC_*` diagnostics, `debug_overlay_*` actions, input logger) are absent from release exports, except Ship Body's `PC_FOOTPRINT_OVERLAP`; the ten `debug_overlay_*` actions are registered only under the dev feature tag and never appear in Settings or rebinding. | Core | PC-2 dev-only, AC-PCI-216 |

## Public surface
- Block `controller.state` (SIM, WORLD persist, PER_PLAYER, SHARED_SUMMARY)
- Commands: `set_move_intent {octant, run}`, `set_aim {aim_angle, live}`, `give_up {actor}`, `stagger {actor}` (SYSTEM origin)
- Hooks: `controller.step` (divisor 1, after `suit.vitals`), `controller.noise` (divisor 1, after `body.integrate`)
- Class B mutators: `set_channel_ref`, `clear_channel_ref`, `set_carry_ref`, `clear_carry_ref`
- Read view: `octant`, `run`, `gait_effective`, `aim_angle`, `aim_live`, `facing`, `loco_state`, `carry_ref`, `salvage_carry`, `channel_ref`, chest point, hand point
- Helpers: `octant_of`, `LocomotionStep.step(state, intent, collide)` (contract; Body implements)
- Presentation signals: MenuInput stream (PC-2a); `inspect_card_context_signal` `{context, inspect_ref}`; `DEVICE_CHANGED`; `cue_input_ignored`
- Inputs owned: `zoom_in`/`zoom_out` (consumed by pipeline), `chart_table` -> `request_pause`
- Knobs/registry names: `V_WALK`, `V_RUN`, `V_CARRY`, `foot_box`, `FOOT_BOX_W/H`, `MOVE_DEADZONE`, `OCTANT_HYSTERESIS_DEG`, `AIM_SEND_INTERVAL`, `ACTION_BUFFER_TICKS`, `RUN_RAMP_TICKS`, `STAGGER_TICKS`, `REACH_PX`
- Diagnostics: `PC_*` channels (dev only)

## Consumes
- Command & Simulation Layer: `submit()`, CR-4/5/7/10/11, `request_pause`, `request_restore`, `push_stimulus(NOISE, actor, class)`, result events with `correlation`, `TICK_RATE`, `tick_alpha`
- Ship Body & Interior Physics: `pos_curr`, `odometer`, `moved(actor)`, `body_of_actor`, `body.integrate`
- Ship Section & Layout Data Model: integer footprint rectangles via Body; `layout.doors`
- Pixel-Perfect Render Pipeline & Camera: `f_q`, screen->picture mapping, zoom ladder, `LOOKAHEAD_RUN_WEIGHT`, `FOLLOW_TAU`, `LAG_CUT`, `LOOKAHEAD_PX`
- Suit & Equipment: `suit.state.locomotion_cap`, `tool_in_hand(player_id)`, `stowed_heavy`; submits `stagger`
- Emitter State & Light-Exposure Query: `lit` bit, `toggle_beam`, `emitter.state` (beam lit, shape), `emitter.place`
- Interaction System: per-object `(command, mode)` declarations, reason classes, `focus_view.press_blocked_moving`, `drop`, `equip_tool`, `throw_glowstick`, `cancel_channel`
- Modular Ship Assembly: `set_channel_ref`/`clear_carry_ref` callers
- Save/Load & Versioned Format: `snapshot`/`restore`/`REBASE_BLOCKS`, `EPOCH_DURABLE`
- Attention System (AT-31) and Horror Entities (HE-33) read `loco_state`
- HUD & Suit Layer: `confirm_view`; Chart Table layer: `ChartPick`, `cursor_hint`
- Settings & Input Rebinding: action map, presets, accessibility options

## Engine risk
- Godot Input / InputMap named actions, `InputEvent` device IDs (`DEVICE_ID_MOUSE`/`DEVICE_ID_KEYBOARD`, 4.7 naming): HIGH (4.7 change; echo flag behavior flagged [UNV])
- `Input.set_mouse_mode` / cursor shape (hidden-confined, visible): LOW
- Physics-callback sampling before `Kernel.step()` (`_physics_process`, fixed 60 Hz tick): LOW
- No CharacterBody2D or physics body: hand-rolled integer kinematics (RefCounted): LOW
- Light2D (chest lamp position/rotation per frame): LOW
- AnimatedSprite2D/Sprite2D integer-position pixel rendering; stretch mode `canvas_items` cursor unit [UNV]: MEDIUM
- Window focus loss/regain notifications and gamepad connect/disconnect (`Input.joy_connection_changed`): LOW
- Renderer `forward_plus` on RM-DECK; Godot 4.7.2 release template: HIGH
- Replication (`SHARED_SUMMARY`, MultiplayerAPI) for VS-B: MEDIUM (deferred scope)
